flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?

And so I kind of notice when the shift happens, it either happens when, you know, he's upset about a toy being taken away, or if he's just overstimulated, I can kind of see the shift in his face where he starts to, you know, feel kind of overwhelmed and he starts very emotional. And so what I tend to do is I, you know, go down to the child's level and I make sure the child can see me and that can see that I am trying to interact with just him in that moment. flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you felt overwhelmed at work with children present. What did you do to manage yourself?

flow_transcript_slices.question: Imagine you’re caring for a child who clearly does not want to be touched during a routine task, like diapering, helping with clothing, or guiding them physically. They are pulling away or saying no. Walk me through exactly what you would do, step by step
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q5 Attempt 1]
I would first take my hands and move my body away from the child. That child is displaying boundaries that he does not want to be crossed, and so I want to respect that. I would also try to explain to him what I'm trying to do, step by step. So if I'm changing a diaper, I'll tell him I'm going to take your diaper off now so you can be clean. And I'm also going to explain why I'm doing what I'm doing, just so that I can have him understand what is happening. And if the child is still setting those boundaries, saying that he doesn't want me around him, I can also ask another co-teacher, somebody else to step in, see if maybe that'll help.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Can you share something you’ve learned about children or yourself over time that changed how you approach your work?

The children will always do, you know, what they want. And even if I intervene or something, they will have full control of who they are.
